scenes.name: 南海·番禺旧帆
scenes.scene: Panyu harbor in the Nanhai realm: a Cantonese lord in a dark muted crimson robe stands beside a clan militia officer on the worn stone quay at left-center, watching a substantial Chinese ocean-going junk depart. Porters bring woven sacks and pottery jars aboard in the middle distance. A shipyard, low grey-tile waterfront roofs and a few battened sails stretch across the Pearl River at right. A small bronze ship gun is visible aboard, subordinate to the scene. Warm late-afternoon sea haze, ochre sailcloth against subdued jade-grey water. Mood: maritime wealth and departing families, a prosperous port under quiet pressure, not a jubilant fleet victory.

scenes.name: 桂林·八桂残疆
scenes.scene: Guilin's diminished realm: from a weathered riverside city wall, lord Feng Yun in a restrained dark scholar's robe and a single armored retainer stand left of center, looking across a winding river toward the distinct steep karst peaks of Guilin. A few laden riverboats and grey-tiled houses inhabit the middle distance; an old mountain watchtower recedes into mist. Keep the human figures appreciable but the beautiful layered karst landscape dominant. Cool blue-green mountains, pearly morning haze, a shaft of warm light on worn stone and the lord's contemplative profile. Mood: loss of territory, enduring water routes and a burden inherited. No ruined apocalyptic city or battle.

scenes.name: 潮州·八邑共推
scenes.scene: Chaozhou council republic: an intimate gathering of about eight elder clan representatives in sober patterned robes and modest Ming-era cloth hats around a long dark wooden table in a southern Chinese ancestral assembly hall. The elected chairman sits at the same level as the others, one elder gestures over closed account ledgers and a plain unlettered seal box; no throne or crown. Angular daylight enters from an open doorway, beyond which a distant red-prowed trading junk and tiled port roofs are visible. Faces and hands form a coherent horizontal conversation across center, with most of the table below them. Warm amber wood, dusty crimson, charcoal and ivory. Mood: mutual dependence, merchant wealth, stern negotiation and a guarded oligarchic compact; not a happy modern meeting.

scenes.name: 客家·山中有国
scenes.scene: Hakka republic defending its mountain home: the young elected militia commander Liao Guanyin-gu in worn indigo cloth and practical lamellar vest consults an older village representative beside the timber-and-rammed-earth gate of a small mountain settlement. A woman carries a grain basket and two spear-bearing villagers stand nearby as equal participants in communal survival. Behind them, modest rectangular rammed-earth houses with grey tiled roofs, narrow terraced fields and layered forest ridges show the small amount of habitable land. No giant round tourist tulou. Diffuse cool dawn with a small warm gate lantern. Indigo, earthy ochre and mist green. Mood: displacement made into belonging, solidarity and resolve before a threatened siege. No battle, massacre, triumphal dictator pose or religious spectacle.

scenes.name: 侬国·众峒举火
scenes.scene: Nong confederation of the Guangxi valleys: village chieftains of Zhuang-Dong cultural background and one Han local notable convene in a sheltered outdoor clearing overlooking a forested valley. Five or six dignified adults wear dark indigo woven cloth, restrained cloth headwraps and practical local dress, one wearing simple lamellar armor. Their leader Nong Mo-na listens rather than sitting on an imperial throne. A weathered bronze drum sits to one side of the central meeting, and a brazier with a small flame lights hands gathered near a low wooden bench. Behind, wood-and-tile stilt dwellings and rice terraces recede into the dusk. Burnished bronze, smoky blue and subdued warm firelight. Mood: victorious former rebels whose independent allies still must agree. Avoid exotic tribal caricature, feathers, fantasy shaman outfits, excessive jewelry, sacrifice, chanting spectacle, invented sacred symbols.

scenes.name: 田州·桂娇遗约
scenes.scene: Tianzhou's inheritance and founding alliance: inside an open-sided timber hall overlooking the green Youjiang valley, the seated aging chieftain Tian Shena discusses a plain closed seal casket with his adult daughter Tian Piyeli, the designated heir. She stands at the same central table, composed and attentive, her hand resting beside the casket rather than wearing a crown. Two local elders observe from either side. Historically grounded Zhuang-Dong indigo woven robes, her restrained hair arrangement and a narrow embroidered sash; practical dignified clothing, no elaborate fantasy costume or sexualization. A small bronze Buddhist devotional figure rests inconspicuously on a side shelf, acknowledging Mahayana faith; distant tiled village roofs outside. Warm diffuse morning light, teak brown, indigo and muted green. Mood: weight of an old alliance and credible female succession; an ongoing discussion, not an already-completed coronation.

scenes.name: 俚寮·高凉旧将
scenes.scene: Gaozhou's veteran between two patrons: Xian Yujie, a mature Cantonese commander in weathered lamellar armor over a dark robe, stands in his fortified gatehouse at center. A southern Chinese civil envoy in a sober burgundy robe approaches from one side, and a Guangxi valley envoy in indigo woven dress and a plain cloth headwrap waits on the other; neither kneels. A closed document case rests between them on a rough table, with a few loyal guards in shadow. Through the gate, low Guangdong hills and settled fields are visible. No overt national symbols, flags or modern maps. Dusty late-day ochre light cuts across three contrasting faces. Mood: a general holding conquered land, diplomatic ambiguity and cautious bargaining; not a battle or a surrender.

scenes.name: 安南·两重冠冕
scenes.scene: Annam's two political identities: ruler Ngo Nghiep Quan (Wu Yequn in the mod), a Vietnamese lord in a restrained muted saffron ceremonial robe and modest late-medieval Vietnamese court headwear, sits within an intimate wooden audience hall in Hue. At center a court official offers an unlettered folded memorial and closed tribute case while another minister quietly watches. Behind the ruler in dim interior light is an ornate but restrained sovereign's seat; outside the open hall beyond a carved wooden column, a distant calm war elephant with its handler crosses a lush palace courtyard. Keep the elephant secondary and plausible scale. Dark red-brown lacquered wood, aged gold, jade greenery, soft tropical light. Mood: outward homage and inward sovereignty, dignity shadowed by defeat and the need for diplomacy. No Qing court costume, no European throne, no modern imperial Hue reconstruction, no enormous fantasy crown or legible script.
